 North Dakota (7-4) hosts Southern Illinois (5-6) at the Alerus Center in a matchup of Missouri Valley Football Conference teams whose recent results have gone in different directions. The Fighting Hawks, ranked No. 10/11 and 4-3 in conference play, won their latest outing 49-21 over Illinois State. Jerry Kaminski threw five touchdown passes and ran for another in that game. The Salukis, 3-4 in the MVFC, lost their latest, so they come in looking to reverse that result on the road.
 Kaminski’s season numbers show a passing attack with real range: 2,481 yards, 27 touchdowns and six interceptions. Deng Deng has 771 receiving yards, and Korey Tai has 37 catches for 486 yards and six scores. The ground game adds Charles Langama with 618 yards and seven touchdowns, and Matt Lawson with 604 yards and four.
 Southern Illinois has its own options. DJ Williams has thrown for 1,869 yards and 11 touchdowns with four interceptions. Kyle Thomas has 710 receiving yards and eight touchdown catches. Chandler Chapman has 614 rushing yards. The Salukis have shown they can win tight games, including a 20-17 result over Northern Iowa that ended on a last-play field goal from a walk-on freshman.

 Game Preview
 Both teams sit in the middle of the MVFC picture, North Dakota at 4-3 in league play and Southern Illinois at 3-4, so the result affects each side’s final conference record. North Dakota has dropped close games to Youngstown State (31-28) and South Dakota (26-23 in overtime), which shows how thin the margins have been. SIU holds a 3-2 edge in all-time meetings but lost its only earlier visit to Grand Forks.

 What to Watch For
 The quarterback matchup frames the game. Kaminski’s 27 touchdown passes against six interceptions give North Dakota a high-scoring look through the air, with Deng, Tai and Caleb Goodloe (16 catches, 209 yards, two touchdowns) as targets. Williams has been more measured, with 11 touchdown passes, but he has Thomas’s eight receiving scores to throw toward. Jake Curry has also played, with 333 yards, four touchdowns and three interceptions.
 The pass rush is the other thing to watch. Braden Mohr has 8.0 sacks for North Dakota, and Ibrahim Sanogo has 7.5 for Southern Illinois, so each quarterback will face a disruptive edge presence. Sebastian Vargas has four interceptions for the Salukis, which matters against a passing game as active as North Dakota’s.
 Southern Illinois’ recent results include a 35-14 loss to Illinois State and a 52-16 loss to South Dakota State. A win in Grand Forks would stand out against both.
